heading_en: Treatment of Guarantees for Purchased Receivables
summary_ja: 購入債権の保証の取扱い、ディスカウントされた購入債権の取扱い及び最劣後の信用補完を提供する信用リスク削減手法の取扱いを定める。
summary_en: Prescribes the treatment of guarantees of purchased receivables, of discounted purchased receivables, and of credit risk mitigation that provides first-loss credit enhancement.
paragraphs: Where a guarantor guarantees, in whole or in part, both the dilution risk and the default risk of purchased receivables, the credit risk-weighted assets for the guarantor may be treated as the credit risk-weighted assets for the guaranteed portion.

Where a guarantor guarantees, in whole or in part, either the dilution risk or the default risk of purchased receivables, the risk weight for the guarantor shall be the risk weight for the guaranteed portion.

Articles 59, 94 and 95 apply mutatis mutandis to the cases referred to in the preceding two paragraphs. In this case, the phrase "Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach" shall be deemed to be replaced with "Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach".

Where the value of purchased receivables has been discounted and one of the events listed in the following items applies, the amount of credit risk-weighted assets may be calculated by the method specified in that item: (i) Where the value of purchased receivables has been discounted in order to provide the most subordinated credit enhancement against losses arising from default risk or dilution risk, and it is agreed that the amount obtained by deducting those losses from the discounted amount (limited to where that amount is positive) will be returned to the transferor of those purchased receivables: a method of treating the discounted portion of the purchased receivables as the most subordinated tranche in a securitization transaction; (ii) Where the value of purchased receivables that were in default at the time of purchase has been discounted, and it is not agreed that the amount obtained by deducting the losses arising from those receivables from the discounted amount (limited to where that amount is positive) will be returned to the transferor of those receivables: a method of recognizing the discounted portion as eligible allowances, limited to the portion not exceeding the expected loss amount of those receivables provided in Article 126.

Where collateral, a partial guarantee or another credit risk mitigation technique with the purchased receivables as the secured claims has been applied in order to provide the most subordinated credit enhancement against losses arising from the default risk or dilution risk of purchased receivables, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach may, in calculating the amount of credit risk-weighted assets of the assets to which that credit risk mitigation technique applies, deem a securitization transaction to have been conducted and treat the credit risk mitigation technique as having been provided to the most subordinated tranche; provided, however, that where the credit risk mitigation technique provides the most subordinated credit enhancement against losses arising from default risk and dilution risk, and the risk weight is calculated, for a securitization exposure whose amount of credit risk-weighted assets is calculated on the assumption that a securitization transaction has been conducted, using the internal ratings-based method prescribed in Division 2 of Subsection 2 of Section 2 of the following Chapter, the weighted average LGD of the underlying assets (LGD) shall, notwithstanding Article 235, paragraph (5), mean the value calculated by the following formula. LGD = (required capital amount for default risk / required capital amount for purchased receivables) × (LGD provided in Article 235, paragraph (5) for default risk) + (required capital amount for dilution risk / required capital amount for purchased receivables) × (100%)

Where a transaction relating to purchased receivables falls under the event listed in paragraph (4), item (i), and the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach is the transferor referred to in that item, that Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach shall treat the discounted portion of the transferred receivables as the most subordinated tranche in a securitization transaction.
